note: Added upstream 2026-11-23. Rescued from intruded.net (formulaone.intruded.net). Levels formulaone0.. via SSH port 2232 (documented on the OTW page; 2232 open live-verified 2026-11-23). Data in /formulaone/. 'The source code for the first level can be accessed by logging in to a wargame hosted on the same server' — figure out which game that is. formulaone0/formulaone0 login DENIED live-verified 2026-11-23 => L0 is a challenge to solve first.

out: daemon on TCP 4091, runs as formulaone0 (not setuid)
reads a byte-compare password (compile-time PASSWD), on success dup2(fd,0/1/2) + system("/bin/sh")
a WRONG byte -> immediate 'WRONG PASSWORD'; a CORRECT byte -> the daemon
blocks in recv for the next byte (no response within 1.5 s) = the oracle

steps.cmd: send the 32-char password, then id + cat /etc/formulaone_pass/formulaone0

levels.note: formulaone0 is a TCP password gate (port 4091) with a byte-by-byte compare whose oracle is the recv() BLOCK: a wrong byte gets an immediate 'WRONG PASSWORD' while a correct byte leaves the daemon blocked reading the next one (no response in 1.5 s). Scanning the alphabet position by position yields the 32-char password in ~32x70 connections. The trailing-'a' artefact past position 32 is the spawned shell swallowing extra bytes (password length found by the scan stopping at 32 with the full string then spawning a shell). Through the dup2-ed /bin/sh: id = uid 20000(formulaone0); cat /etc/formulaone_pass/formulaone0 = the same string = the SSH login password for formulaone0 on port 2232. Verified by ssh login (uid=20000). Recording: recordings/formulaone/L0.cast. Files: tools/formulaone/l0/ (solve.py).
